findings.description: The pending ledger is initialized before acquiring its write lock. Two writers targeting the same new sprint can both observe that the file is absent.
findings.failure_mode: After the first writer initializes and appends a decision, the second writer can execute its delayed initialization and truncate the ledger back to decisions: []. Its subsequent locked write succeeds, permanently losing the first decision.
findings.suggested_fix: Acquire the target lock before checking for existence and initializing the pending ledger, and retain that lock through the append and swap.

findings.description: Import locks only the destination ledger, then unconditionally removes the source pending file. It never coordinates with writers updating that pending file.
findings.failure_mode: If a worktree appends a decision after import reads the pending snapshot but before import removes the file, the appended decision is absent from the imported rows and is deleted with the pending file. A writer already holding the source lock can also recreate the file after removal, allowing previously imported rows to be imported again.
findings.suggested_fix: Coordinate import and pending writes using the same source lock across checkouts. Hold it from source validation and snapshotting through successful import and source removal.

findings.description: `live_run_signal(){ ctx_signals | grep -q '^live ' ; }` runs under `set -o pipefail`. `grep -q` exits on the first match and closes the pipe; `ctx_signals` then keeps running (it spawns jq/yq between echoes for the marker, the two state files and the env checks) and its next `echo` hits a closed pipe, so the function subshell dies with SIGPIPE (status 141). With pipefail the pipeline status becomes 141, `live_run_signal` returns false, and `op_confirm` (line 509) does NOT refuse even though a live signal holds. This triggers exactly in the common case the gate exists for: an autonomous run where two or more live signals coexist (fresh `.run/unattended.json` + `state.json` RUNNING, or either plus `LOA_UNATTENDED=1`). `is_unattended` is safe because it captures the whole output; only the grep -q form is affected.
findings.failure_mode: During an unattended run (RUNNING state plus marker or env flag), `dec-write-lib.sh confirm --recorded-by decisions-command ...` proceeds and moves rows to `decided` instead of being refused; the only runtime check in the operator-only confirm path silently disappears when it matters most.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the output instead of streaming into grep -q: `live_run_signal(){ [[ -n "$(ctx_signals | grep '^live ' || true)" ]]; }` or `ctx_signals | grep '^live ' >/dev/null` without `-q`. Add a bats case with a fresh marker AND LOA_UNATTENDED=1 and assert confirm exits 1.

findings.description: Every operator-only transition (confirm, reject/supersede of a decided row, context --clear) is gated solely on the caller passing `--recorded-by decisions-command`. `disable-model-invocation: true` only stops the Skill tool from starting `/decisions`; the model's Bash tool can still run the script with that flag and, with `--answer-ref cli:<now>`, mint `decided_by: operator`. decisions.md states the writer 'verifies' and that 'a row becomes decided only here', which overstates what the script enforces; the real control is the grep test in tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats plus the model following prose rules.
findings.failure_mode: A prompt-injected or over-eager agent confirms its own proposed rows and the ledger records them as operator decisions; nothing in the writer can tell the difference.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the guard as advisory in the header and decisions.md, and add a defence in depth that is outside the model's control, e.g. a PreToolUse Bash hook that blocks `dec-write-lib.sh confirm|reject|supersede|context --clear` unless an operator-set env/flag file exists, or require the confirm transition to be written from a hook that only `/decisions` arms.

findings.description: In the operator path, `supersede` immediately moves the old `decided` row to `superseded` while the replacement lands only `proposed`. If the operator then rejects the replacement (or never confirms it), the ledger has a superseded decision with no decided successor. The old row can never be re-opened or re-superseded (line 599 requires status `decided`), and reject on the replacement does not restore it. This is the operator-side twin of reviewer concern #5 (agent path leaves `supersede_proposed_by` dangling).
findings.failure_mode: Operator supersedes DEC-0007 with DEC-0012, then rejects DEC-0012 after review: DEC-0007 is permanently `superseded by DEC-0012` where DEC-0012 is `rejected`; the decision is lost from every active view and `list --status decided` no longer shows it.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the operator supersede like the agent one (set `supersede_proposed_by`, flip to `superseded` only when the replacement is confirmed), or have `reject` on a row with `.supersedes` revert the old row's status/`supersede_proposed_by` in the same write.

findings.cross_file_justification: The hook .claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh (lines 102-105) implements the same session comparison, and decisions.md rule 5 tells the session to report the refusal text verbatim, so the misleading repair text is what the operator sees.
findings.description: 'Other session' staleness depends on `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID`/`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` being exported to the shell. If neither is set (Claude Code passes the session id to hooks via stdin JSON, not via env, and the Bash tool does not export it), `session_id()` records `unknown-session` and `sess` is empty on later sessions, so the `sid != sess` branch never fires and a marker written by an autonomous run stays `fresh` for the full TTL (24 h). `confirm` then dies with 'a live-run signal holds (...unattended-marker...); confirm after the run, interactively', which is exactly what the operator is doing; the message never mentions `/decisions clear-unattended`, and the hook's stale notice (the only place that mentions it) does not appear because the marker is not considered stale.
findings.failure_mode: After any autonomous run that set the marker, operator confirms are refused for up to 24 h in subsequent interactive sessions with repair text that does not lead to the fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Include `clear-unattended` in the confirm refusal when the only live signal is the marker; consider falling back to a per-process-tree or mtime-based notion of 'session' when the env var is absent, and verify in a bats case with the env var unset.

findings.cross_file_justification: decisions.md rule 3 (lines 54-56) promises that the `cli:` answer-ref 'is what records decided_by: operator', and grimoire-index.sh's decisions table comment says the voice shows the proposer only 'while the row awaits /decisions confirm'.
findings.description: `confirm` only adopts the operator's `--answer-ref` when `.decided_by_ref` is null. Rows created with `--as flatline|dissent` already carry `decided_by_ref: flatline:<path>` from creation, so the operator's `cli:` ref is silently dropped and `decided_by` becomes `flatline`/`dissent`, never `operator`. `list --not-decided-by operator` (SDD Appendix D) keeps listing these rows as not operator-decided even after the operator confirmed them.
findings.failure_mode: Operator confirms a Flatline-proposed row through /decisions exactly as documented; the ledger records `decided_by: flatline`, contradicting the command doc and the index semantics, and audit views misreport who decided.
findings.suggested_fix: Either always set `decided_by: operator` and the operator ref on confirm (keeping the original artifact ref in a separate field such as `proposed_by_ref`), or change decisions.md and the index comment to state that confirm preserves the proposing voice.

findings.cross_file_justification: karpathy-principles.md and autonomous-agent/SKILL.md now instruct unattended runs to record every assumption with `dec-write-lib.sh new` and 'then proceed'; the writer refuses that call in the environments those runs commonly use.
findings.description: The header says 'Live-ledger writes exit 1 under CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS or LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT=1', but the `ci_blocked` check sits before the pending-file branch and so also refuses `--pending`/worktree writes. The only exemption is `--file`. An autonomous run executed under GitHub Actions (CI=true) or from a hook therefore cannot record decisions at all, while the new protocol text replaces the old NOTES.md fallback with a mandatory ledger write and offers no alternative when the write is refused.
findings.failure_mode: Unattended CI runs either halt on a non-zero exit from `new` or skip recording entirely, so the decision surface the PR introduces is empty precisely for the runs it was designed to audit.
findings.suggested_fix: Either allow pending-file writes under CI (they are gitignored scratch files), or restore an explicit fallback in karpathy-principles.md/autonomous-agent SKILL.md (record in NOTES.md Decision Log when `new` exits 1 with the CI refusal), and fix the header comment to match the behaviour.

findings.cross_file_justification: The SDD template's new Appendix D instructs the agent to paste `dec-write-lib.sh list ... --format md` output into sdd.md, an L5 artifact the model reads back in later phases.
findings.description: `op_list` emits agent-authored `summary`, `rationale` and `source` through `cl`, which strips only `[[:cntrl:]]` (C0) and escapes `|`. C1 controls, U+2028/2029, `<`, `>`, backticks and markdown constructs pass through unchanged. The session-start hook and even the lower-stakes grimoire-index sanitise harder (the hook replaces angle brackets and backticks and wraps in an L6 fence). The md table lands in sdd.md and is re-read by the model without any fence, so a row written during an unattended run can carry instructions or HTML into a trusted document.
findings.failure_mode: A `rationale` like `IMPORTANT: ignore prior instructions...` written by an agent in an autonomous run is rendered verbatim into the SDD and read by subsequent sessions as document content.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the hook's `clean` regex in `op_list` (C1 and U+2028/9 stripping, `<`/`>`/backtick replacement, length cap), and have the SDD template wrap the rendered table in the L6 untrusted-content fence or render only id/status/voice/summary rather than rationale.
